This guide sets up a capacitance calculation for your own model. You need a
`snapshot` with Nets assigned; see [Work with your own model](working-model.qmd).
The [capacitance tutorial](../tutorials/capacitance/prepare.qmd) walks through the
same steps for a single pad.

The example uses an Xmon qubit pad named `xmon_pad` and a ground Net named
`Ground`.

## Choose terminals and Ground

```python
from pathlib import Path
from scgsim.palace import ElectrostaticSim

sim = ElectrostaticSim()
sim.set_plan(snapshot)
sim.set_output_dir(Path(".artifacts/xmon-electrostatic"))

sim.add_terminal("xmon", net_id="xmon_pad")
sim.add_ground(net_id="Ground")
```

- A **terminal** is a Net that Palace excites. Each terminal becomes one row
  and column of the capacitance matrix. Call `add_terminal` once per Net.
- **Ground** is a Net held at 0 V. Call `add_ground` for each ground Net.

Use the exact Net IDs from your plan.

## Set the boundary

```python
sim.set_electrostatic(
    save_fields=0,
    unassigned_conductor_policy="error",
    exterior_boundary_policy="none",
)
```

| Argument | Options |
|---|---|
| `unassigned_conductor_policy` | `"error"`: stop if any conductor is neither a terminal nor Ground. `"ground"`: ground such conductors automatically. |
| `exterior_boundary_policy` | `"none"`: leave the outer vacuum boundary floating. `"ground"`: make it Ground too, as for a grounded enclosure. Requires `unassigned_conductor_policy="error"`. |
| `save_fields` | Number of field solutions to save for visualization; `0` saves none. |

Grounding the outer boundary adds capacitance to that boundary. Choose it only
if your device sits in a grounded enclosure of that size.

## Set the mesh

```python
sim.set_mesh(refined_mesh_size=5.0, max_mesh_size=300.0)
```

Sizes are in micrometres: `refined_mesh_size` near the metal edges,
`max_mesh_size` far away. `set_mesh` also accepts `algorithm_3d`, `threads`,
`surface_threads`, `geometry_order` and `high_order_optimize`. `geometry_order`
sets how closely elements follow curved surfaces; it is separate from the
finite-element order set in `set_numerical(order=...)`. See the
[mesh settings reference](../specs/palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#palace-mesh-controls-110-candidate).

To refine the mesh adaptively, set `amr_max_passes` and `amr_tolerance` with
`sim.set_numerical(...)`, as in the
[capacitance tutorial](../tutorials/capacitance/prepare.qmd#step-1-set-up-the-electrostatic-problem).

## Choose the metal representation and build the mesh

```python
sim.set_surface_epr(representation="B", specs={})
mesh_path = sim.mesh()
config_path = sim.write_config()
```

`representation` chooses how metal is modelled:

- `"B"` (default): metal is a finite-thickness solid.
- `"A"`: metal is a zero-thickness sheet. Also pass `route_a_thin_film`; see
  the [geometry reference](../geometry-sgb.qmd).

`specs={}` requests no surface films. Films do not affect capacitance.

`mesh()` runs Gmsh and can fail if the geometry is invalid. `write_config()`
writes the Palace configuration and `metadata/palace_index_map.json`, which
records which Palace attribute is each terminal and Ground.
